examples.what_they_do: Copy/badge: The tool emphasizes an explicit approximation and a helpful vibe; placement: near the top of the “Understanding generated images” section in the help article; balance: frames the output as a visual aid not a guarantee, with direct caveats about accuracy and fit.

Copy/badge: “Represented results are for illustrative purposes only. Individual results will vary.”; placement: within the VTO/terms area, not on the live result card; balance: uses concise, direct language to set expectations while still enabling exploration.

Copy/badge: no explicit approximation badge observed in the historical gallery; placement: product-specific controls (Tap Bar, Product Filter, Shade Comparison) presented as functional UI; balance: confidence grounded in product-specific shade matching and controls rather than a generic “similar look” substitute.

Copy/badge: claims like “3D representations” and “true to scale” with explicit catalog-item linkage; placement: on official AR-placement announcements; balance: relies on named SKU and catalog identity to support confidence without implying generated content.

Copy/badge: on-image label “Imagined with AI” with visible markers + metadata; placement: on the image itself as a provenance cue; balance: concise, affirmative provenance rather than warning-heavy language.

recommendations: AI SIMILAR-LOOK PREVIEW: Use a persistent, on-image badge that clearly marks generated content as a preview (e.g., AI SIMILAR-LOOK PREVIEW).

Style inspiration only — this AI-generated preview, not the actual garment: Place an immediately visible, one-line caption under or beside the preview image to disambiguate content from purchasable inventory.

Shop real matching pieces: Under the preview, include a visually distinct inventory divider with a note that fabric, print, drape, color, and size may differ from the preview; link to real SKUs from local curators.

Find a verified match: Provide a prominent CTA near the preview (and again in WhatsApp/M-Pesa handoff) that clarifies the user is selecting a real item from live stock (SKU, price, size, and stock shown) rather than purchasing the AI image.

No exact item available: If no exact item exists, show a clear fallback like “No exact item available. Here are real pieces with a similar style you can buy now,” ensuring users are steered toward verifiable inventory with local payment options.
value.topic: Labeling AI-generated approximations in consumer interfaces (fashion/beauty/AR) to maintain trust and conversion while avoiding misleading representations.
